messages:
laura: brief recap from the backfill run this morning: we saw ~14% of hotstarts take a slow-path because the shards had no sidecar index. we also hit a couple of OOMs when parsing headers in-parallel. want to discuss a conservative rollout for stub files + GC semantics.

sam: thanks. can you share perf numbers? e.g., cold start P50/P95 with manifest vs stub vs indexless scans?

laura: quick numbers from staging (4x A100 workers):
- indexed manifest hotstart: p50 48ms, p95 110ms
- stub (offset-only) hotstart: p50 55ms, p95 150ms
- indexless range-scan hotstart: p50 200ms, p95 800ms (and heavy memory)
so stubs give near parity for p50, acceptable p95.

nate: sounds good. rollout plan: read-only acceptance first (loader accepts stubs), then backfill writer phased in. For GC: when a full manifest appears, retire stub. Avoid race windows where stub and manifest disagree.

irene: propose retirement invariant: stub.valid_until is set to the manifest.creation_ts when manifest appears; loader prefers manifest if creation_ts >= stub.valid_since. we also need to handle shard re-uploads where ETag changes.

anya: quick question on storage: do stubs live in the same bucket/prefix as shards? if yes, listing might be expensive for large model catalogs. maybe keep stubs in a separate prefix with objects named by shard path -> stub. that makes GC scanning simpler.

greg: separate prefix also helps policy enforcement (lifecycle rules). my $0.02: write stubs to /stubs/<model>/<shard>.stub.json and keep a tombstone api that records replacements.

sam: we also need a compact GC that doesn't re-list full model catalogs; use work-queue driven GC: backfill job pushes a message when it completes manifest generation; GC worker consumes and deletes stub. fallback periodic reconciliation for missed events.

laura: noted. also thought about stub TTL. If stub.age > 7d and no manifest, we schedule a higher-priority manifestization job. avoids long-term reliance on stubs.

nate: provenance checks: loader MUST check stub.etag == object.etag before trusting offsets. If mismatch -> invalidate stub and fallback to range-scan (or try to re-fetch manifest). This avoids silently reading stale offsets.

irene: agree. add a fast verification: HEAD object and compare ETag before warmup. For high QPS routes this adds an extra HEAD per-hotstart; cost?

laura: measured HEAD cost in staging: ~6ms median in same region; acceptable for P50 but it bumps p95 slightly. we could cache ETag in a small LRU for 30s to avoid repeated HEADs for very bursty workloads.

anya: metrics/telemetry: add counters for stub-accepted, stub-rejected(etag-mismatch), stub-evicted(gc), stub-aged-triggered, stub-manifest-converted. console should expose backlog of stubs per-model.

greg: security check: ensure stub content is canonicalized and signed by backfill process (HMAC) to avoid accidental tampering if object store allows public writes. also log who created the stub.

nate: HMAC makes sense if we worry about untrusted writers. for now internal backfill jobs run with a service principal; log+audit should be sufficient. HMAC can be optional v0.2.

laura: UX question: catalog presentation. Anya suggested index_state = [indexed, stubbed, none]. We also might display stub_age and stub_etag. that helps on-call decide whether to trigger manifestization.

sam: edge-case: multipart uploads in S3 produce temporary ETags; we must ensure we only trust stubs after finalization of the multipart upload. packager/backfill should wait for object completion before writing stub. add precondition in stub writer: `if-match` or require object size+etag to be stable.

irene: also handle gzipped shard archives where offsets are not stable across compressions; stub should only be allowed for format types that support byte-range offsets (i.e., raw safetensors, not compressed tar). Block stub generation for incompatible encodings.

laura: good catch. we'll gate stub writability on artifact.format in catalog (raw/safetensors-v1 allowed).

deploy-bot: deploy in staging: feature/stub-gc -> 2026-04-02T02:30Z :rocket: (includes stub read + gc worker skeleton)

laura: summary of consensus:
- implement compact .stub.json with fields: version, shard_index, offsets[], etag, created_ts
- loader verifies etag via HEAD and accepts stub only if match (with short LRU cache)
- backfill writes stubs to a dedicated prefix with atomic tmp->rename pattern; waits for object finalization
- GC is event-driven (backfill posts message) with periodic reconciliation; stubs older than 7d escalate manifest jobs
- metrics: stub_accept/reject/age/gc/convert counters + catalog index_state and stub_age/etag shown in console
- security: audit log on creation; HMAC optional in v0.2

laura: action items (short):
- Sam: add HEAD+LRU caching and accept-only-read-side by EOW
- Anya: console fields + metrics spec by midweek
- Nate: stub etag invariant and multi-upload checks
- Irene: add format whitelist and atomic write pattern to loader docs
- Greg: GC worker skeleton and event schema

laura: I'll capture this in an RFC + a short compatibility note for older loaders. thanks all, this feels low-risk and high-value. ping if anything else. :thumbsup:
